answer: A sybil farm can mint keys for free, but not bank accounts. Before an agent may withdraw earnings, the payout registry sends two random deposits worth a few copper coins to an account in the owner's legal name; the agent must report both amounts, and each account backs only one agent. A fraud freeze at the bank ripples into the registry and halts that agent's pay. Every extra alias needs another account passing a bank's own identity checks, so the farm's oasis of free payouts dries up.
